clue.text: Put income right, hopefully with this

definitions.text: Put income right, hopefully with this

parts.words: Put income right, hopefully with this
parts.note: the machine you might use to sort out your tax and income figures; the letters of 'put' and 'come' play on its spelling too

explanation.surface: Advice on getting one's finances in order with the help of some tool.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a pun too: split 'income' as IN COME, and PUT placed in COME, plus R for right, spells the machine; a leaf cannot split one printed word, so it stands as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A home electronic machine is the device people use to calculate and correct their accounts.

clue.text: Dynasty put up with bloodsucker

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means its letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Tang were a Chinese ruling dynasty

explanation.surface: An ancient ruling family tolerating a biting insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This small flying insect bites and feeds on blood, so it is a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Sleeping accommodation could formerly be found in Mid-Glamorgan

parts.note: a bed is where you sleep
was is the past tense of 'be', what formerly could be

explanation.surface: A bed of the kind once found in a Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-Glamorgan was a county in South Wales; the answer is a small town there, near Caerphilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The place named is a real town located in that former Welsh county, so it is found there.

clue.text: With his tools, Gordius has to be thoughtful

parts.note: a crossword setter's tools are pens
the setter Gordius says 'I've' for 'I have'

explanation.surface: The setter reflects on his trade, claiming his pens make him reflective.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius is the setter of this puzzle, so 'Gordius has' is 'I have', contracted to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive is a synonym for deep in reflection, quietly meditative.

clue.text: Baby dunked by his mother in water turning cold

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, so cold goes inside water
turning signals the word for water is written backwards

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a chill is a coldness

explanation.surface: A mother plunges her infant into chilly water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes AES from the word for water, and 'in' puts the cold inside it. In Greek myth the sea-nymph Thetis dipped her infant son in the River Styx, holding him by the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was dipped in the Styx as an infant by his mother Thetis to make him invulnerable.

clue.text: Reactionary fellow involved in flagrant agitation about incomer from elsewhere

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the shuffled letters surround the incomer
agitation stirs up the letters of the word before it

parts.note: ET is the extra-terrestrial, a visitor from another world

explanation.surface: A bigot is stirred up by an outsider arriving in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' rearranges the letters, 'about' wraps them round the alien. The answer is the bigoted East Ender of the British sitcom Till Death Us Do Part.
explanation.definitionFit: The TV character is famous as a ranting reactionary, a byword for bigoted conservatism.

clue.text: Conference in a nasty uprising

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, uprising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bad is a synonym for nasty

explanation.surface: A meeting caught up in an ugly revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' gives DABA, set after IN. The answer is a word from southern Africa for a meeting of elders or council.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a southern African term for a conference or gathering to discuss matters.

clue.text: Stick together as indicated by ticket machine?

definitions.meaning: to be united, to cohere as one
read as two words it is the instruction a ticket machine shows: put money in at this point

explanation.definitionFit: Coinhere is a rare verb meaning to cohere or stick together; split, it is a machine's instruction.

clue.text: Mark of short settlement

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a colony is a settlement

explanation.surface: A sign of a brief agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark of two dots.

clue.text: See spinners return

indicators.note: return means the letters come back the other way

parts.note: tops are spinning toys

explanation.surface: Watch the slow bowlers come back.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, spinners are slow bowlers, which the surface suggests; here they are toys.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Spooner's flamboyant manner as occasion for soap

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: dashing means stylish and flamboyant
a way is a manner

explanation.surface: Someone's showy style is a cue for lathering up.
explanation.definitionFit: The day set aside for the laundry is an occasion for using soap.

clue.text: Lots of food on board

annotationWithheld.why: Lots of food on board (6): STACKS is S(TACK)S, but 'on board' must both give SS and signal the insertion, one phrase doing two jobs

clue.text: Tea is served with bread and a hunk of meat

indicators.note: served with reads as tea and is being served around the bread and a, enclosing them

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
taken as written
a roll is a piece of bread

explanation.surface: A meal of tea, a bread roll and a chunk of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a heavy French breed of sheep (or cattle) raised for meat; 'hunk of meat' describes the beast loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: This French breed is a big, heavily muscled meat animal, so loosely a hunk of meat.

clue.text: Emperor's goodbye before rain shower

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: shower read as one who shows: it presents the word's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler bids farewell before a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian was a third-century Roman emperor, captured by the Persians.

clue.text: Call to account a shower, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: Blaming a passing downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to bring someone before a court to answer a charge, holding them to account.

clue.text: Flyers able to go over Belshazzar's vision?

indicators.note: go goes over, around, the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, are flyers
fit means able

explanation.surface: Pilots able to fly over a Babylonian king's dream?
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Belshazzar saw a hand write on his palace wall, so the 'vision' was wall writing, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffito is the singular of graffiti, writing on a wall like the Biblical writing on the wall.

clue.text: Taste is missing to some extent in irony

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Irony lacks a certain refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteism is a rhetorical term for polite, witty irony or ingenious mockery.

clue.text: Toast for the lady by a college servant

parts.note: a scout is a servant at an Oxford college
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A toast to a woman, raised by a college porter.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOUT is the name for a college servant at Oxford. The answer is a Scots word meaning to scorch or toast lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouther is a Scottish verb meaning to scorch or toast slightly.

clue.text: Gamble holds fine possibility, which is a help

indicators.note: holds means the gamble surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

indicators.note: possibility suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A punt with a good chance of paying off would be welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibility' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of 'fine' are one possible arrangement among others. 'holds' puts the result inside the gamble, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage or help, something that does you good.

clue.text: Noble list with exclusion of the elderly

parts.note: a bar on something is an exclusion of it
age stands for old people, the aged

explanation.surface: A list of nobles discriminating against older people.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronage is the body of barons, or a published roll of the nobility.

clue.text: Programme for article on oral sex

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: oral means it is spoken: its sound gives the letters

parts.note: gender is a person's sex

explanation.surface: A schedule including a discussion of a sexual act.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the final R of the word for sex is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme or list of business for a meeting.

clue.text: Poet could require a vote

definitions.meaning: Andrew ... was the British Poet Laureate
a proposal put before a meeting that may need a vote

explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Motion was Poet Laureate, and a formal proposal at a meeting may be put to a vote.

clue.text: Bringing up a setter, perhaps, setter's about to change

indicators.note: about means the setter's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: my

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a setter is a dog, and Fido is a stock dog's name

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, raising a dog, is about to alter things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing up' gives ODIF, and 'about' wraps the possessive round it. Setters say 'I' or 'my' for themselves; the surface's 'setter' is the dog breed in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify is to change or alter something.

clue.text: Convey property for nuclear generation

parts.note: to convey property legally is to sell it
a field is a piece of property

explanation.surface: Selling land for an atomic power station.
explanation.walkthrough: SELLAFIELD is the nuclear site in Cumbria, NW England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian site generated nuclear power and reprocesses nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Correctly reported ceremony

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the sound counts

parts.note: right means correctly

explanation.surface: A ritual described accurately.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ceremony or ritual.

clue.text: Way one's said to have gone by boat?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: rowed means went by oar-powered boat

explanation.surface: A route someone claims to have travelled by water?
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a way or route.

clue.text: Tendency of doctor to make fit

indicators.note: to make, as in remake, signals the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A physician's habit of getting people healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of something is its general tendency or direction.

clue.text: Rare find unfortunately can't be seen

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, a rare discovery is invisible.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared light lies beyond the visible spectrum, so it is invisible to the eye.
